repo.name: g6
repo.description: ♾ A Graph Visualization Framework in JavaScript.

readme.summary: Strong introduction and quick-start, but relies heavily on external docs for configuration depth, examples, and troubleshooting.
readme.top_issue: No troubleshooting section and minimal configuration documentation — users hit any issue must leave to external docs.

common_complaints: Edge creation visual glitches and offset bugs
Performance degradation with large datasets (many edges)
Layout and positioning issues (node rotation, tree ordering)
sentiment.summary: Mixed health: Active issue tracking and recent labeling indicate ongoing maintenance, but multiple critical unresolved bugs (Vue 3 TypeError, edge creation offsets, UI stuttering) with months-old open dates and 'waiting for maintainer' backlogs suggest slow response times and possible feature creep outpacing team capacity.

communication.summary: The maintainer responses are generally helpful, clear, and patient. They provide explanations for the 'why' behind some decisions but could delve deeper in technical details. New contributors are encouraged, and the communication style is welcoming.

concerns: 330 open issues with zero closed in past 6 months indicates no issue triage or maintenance
Zero merged PRs in 6 months shows no active development or contributions being integrated
No active contributors for 6 months suggests abandonment by maintainers
Unknown last release date raises questions about versioning and release cycle
Long period of inactivity before recent February commit indicates inconsistent maintenance
positive_signals: One recent commit on 2026-02-11 suggests the project is not completely abandoned
maintenance.summary: The project is stale with 330 unresolved issues, zero PRs merged in 6 months, and no active contributors despite minimal recent activity.

changelog.summary: The changelog is well-categorized and appears comprehensive, but lacks clear marking of breaking changes and migration guides.

project_metrics.description: ♾ A Graph Visualization Framework in JavaScript.

concerns: High number of open issues (294) which could indicate unresolved problems or a backlog that needs attention.
highlights: Regular commits and releases, with 35 commits and one release in the past six months. Active contributor community with 18 contributors over the same period.
